crop.notes: Clipping runs from the Helen Bertram whooping-cough article (top) into the end of Macon McCormick's boxing column (Irish fights, Dan Stuart, Corbett, Kid McCoy). Only the final subsection 'Allen and Joe Goss' (crops 6-7) is about Allen; it is complete.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Republic ran Macon McCormick's boxing column, in which a gentleman recalled that Tom Allen, fearing for his life, deliberately fouled Joe Goss in Kentucky, and Goss offered to fight on before the referee gave him the win.

metadata.notes: Masthead: The Republic, St. Louis, Mo., Sunday Morning, August 8, 1897, page 6. Column is special correspondence from New York.

facts.fact: A recollection printed in 1897 said that in his fight with Joe Goss in Kentucky near Cincinnati, Allen, seeing his life in danger from Goss's backers, deliberately struck a foul blow; Goss offered to fight on but the referee awarded the fight to Goss

notes: Secondhand account from an unnamed gentleman, written about 21 years after the fight; the article gives no date for the fight (1876 is from the fight record).
